newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan blasts China's protest at tourism meeting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan blasts China's protest at tourism meeting.

text.p: Taiwan slammed rival China on Thursday for its efforts to block Taipei's attendance at an international tourism meeting in the Philippines, saying it was now boycotting the meeting.
"We have decided not to participate in the meeting as protest," a Taiwan tourism bureau official told Reuters.
"They should not have mingled politics with tourism. We are extremely dissatisfied with communist China's move," the official said by telephone.
Taipei's delegation did not show up at the meeting's opening on Thursday following Beijing's bitter complaints that Manila had no business inviting Taiwan in the first place.

Since a civil war split them in 1949, China has seen Taiwan as a renegade province with no right to join international gatherings and organisations as a sovereign state, though it tolerates unofficial participation under some circumstances.
Beijing assailed Manila's decision to invite an official Taiwan delegation as a violation of the "one-China" pledge that underlies the Philippines' diplomatic relations with China.
Taiwan has no diplomatic relations with the Philippines, though they enjoy extensive trade, investment and tourism ties.
Officials said the Philippine tourism department invited Taiwan without checking with the foreign ministry.
Some 60 countries are attending the two-day meeting of the World Tourism Organisation, which is looking at some of the darker uses of mass travel, including drugs, prostitution and child abuse.
